approaches.name: Anterolateral humeral shaft (after Henry)
selection_indications: Useful for anterior/anterolateral plate application, especially proximal and middle-shaft patterns; distal extension depends on fixation requirements.
selection_limitations: Approach and plate surface must be selected according to fracture level, morphology, radial nerve pathology, and required fixation length.
positioning: Supine or beach-chair positioning is used for anterior or anterolateral plating.
exposure: Develop the interval along the lateral border of biceps, identify the radial nerve between biceps/brachialis and the mobile wad distally, and split or mobilize brachialis while preserving its innervation.

structures_at_risk.protection: Identify its distal interval and course through the lateral intermuscular septum; avoid hazardous blind Hohmann placement in the distal humerus.

structures_at_risk.structure: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm
structures_at_risk.protection: Identify where it crosses the distal field.

pitfalls: Failure to document and protect the radial nerve across the plate
questions: Q: Where is the radial nerve found distally in the anterolateral exposure? A: It is identified between the brachialis/biceps side and the mobile wad and followed toward the lateral intermuscular septum.
Q: Why can brachialis be split? A: Its dual innervation permits a controlled split, but indiscriminate retraction can still injure nerve branches.
approaches.coverage_notes: The exact exposure length and plate surface are fracture-specific.

approaches.name: Posterior humeral shaft (triceps-split or triceps-on)
selection_indications: Provides access to the posterior surface for posterior plating; particularly useful when distal posterior fixation or direct radial nerve assessment is required.
selection_limitations: Positioning and triceps management differ between split and triceps-sparing variants.
positioning: Prone or lateral decubitus positioning is normally used for posterior plating.
exposure: Develop the selected posterior triceps-split or triceps-on plane and identify/protect the radial nerve with the profunda brachii where they cross the posterior humerus before plate passage.

structures_at_risk.risk_phase: Deep posterior exposure and plate placement
structures_at_risk.protection: Identify the bundle, avoid traction, and document its relationship to the final plate.

pitfalls: Passing a plate without establishing the radial nerve relationship
Excessive traction on the nerve during reduction
questions: Q: What accompanies the radial nerve in the posterior humeral exposure? A: The profunda brachii vessels accompany it in the spiral groove.
Q: What should be documented at the end of plating? A: The radial nerve's relationship to the plate and the postoperative nerve examination.
approaches.coverage_notes: Posterior split and triceps-sparing variants should be distinguished in the case plan.
